topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: These opening remarks link the lecture to histopathology practicals and outline the key learning outcomes regarding cancer genetics and cellular transformation.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Assays of Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and detail the laboratory assays used to detect cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of cancer mutations and illustrate their biochemical and genetic mechanisms using the Rb cell-cycle checkpoint and p53 as examples.

topics.label: Defects Underlying Sequence and Chromosomal Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the molecular causes of genomic instability arising from failures in DNA repair pathways, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation.

topics.label: Multi-Step Progression, Hereditary Cancer Predisposition, and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential somatic and inherited mutations drive tumor development, hereditary cancer syndromes, and therapy-induced tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding remarks summarize the session, invite student questions, and recommend supplementary reading on cancer biology.
